title: Canonical site-section pullback is normalized by comparison units and replacements
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites in the common universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be continuous and cocontinuous [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor](1), and let $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ be its induced geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Write $L=g^{-1}:\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$, also for its termwise and exact derived extensions. Use the ordinary bounded-below derived categories, localization $Q$, and cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. For a site object $V$, let $\alpha^V_K:Q\Gamma(V,K)\to R\Gamma(V,QK)$ be the ordinary right-derived comparison unit [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], for a bounded-below complex $K$ on that site. Fix $U\in\mathcal C$. Let $e_F:\Gamma(U,LF)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(u(U),F)$ be the identity on sections given by precomposition, with $e_K$ its termwise version on complexes. There is a unique natural transformation
$$\tau:R\Gamma(u(U),-)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(U,L(-))$$
characterized, on every bounded-below complex $K$ of abelian sheaves on $\mathcal D$, by
$$\tau_{QK}\circ\alpha^{u(U)}_K=\alpha^U_{LK}\circ Q(e_K^{-1}).$$
It is the ordinary derived pullback of sections. If $I$ is any bounded-below complex of injective abelian sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and $r:LI\to J$ is any quasi-isomorphism to a bounded-below complex of injective abelian sheaves on $\mathcal C$, then in $D^+(\operatorname{Ab})$ its component satisfies
$$\tau_{QI}\circ\alpha^{u(U)}_I=R\Gamma(U,(Qr)^{-1})\circ\alpha^U_J\circ Q\Gamma(U,r)\circ Q(e_I^{-1})=\alpha^U_{LI}\circ Q(e_I^{-1}).$$
Here $\alpha^{u(U)}_I$ and $\alpha^U_J$ are the injective-complex computation isomorphisms; the formula does not assume that $LI$ is termwise injective or that $Q\Gamma(U,r)$ is invertible. For every $\rho:QI\cong M$, transport by $R\Gamma(u(U),\rho)$ and $R\Gamma(U,L\rho)$ gives the component $\tau_M$, independent of $I,J,r,\rho$. Thus these formulas commute with all coefficient morphisms in $D^+(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal D))$ and identify the same transformation for any uniquely isomorphic choice of the right-derived functors and their comparison units.

proof.text: Put $S=R\Gamma(u(U),-)$ and $T=R\Gamma(U,-)\circ L$ on $D^+(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal D))$. The site-sheaves theorem makes both abelian sheaf categories abelian with enough injectives; evaluation is additive by the sites-and-cohomology definition. The continuous-cocontinuous adjunction identifies the underlying set sheaf of $LF$ with $F\circ u$. Its identity on sections respects addition and coefficient maps, hence gives the additive natural isomorphism $e$. The geometric-inverse-image theorem supplies exactness of $L$, with the sites interchanged to match $g$. Exactness gives $H^n(LK)=L H^n(K)$ (preservation of kernels, images and cokernels), so termwise $L$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and boundedness below. Thus its stipulated derived extension and the composite $T$ are well defined.

For each bounded-below complex $K$ set $\beta_K=\alpha^U_{LK}\circ Q(e_K^{-1})$. For a complex map $f:K\to K'$, naturality of $e$ and of $\alpha^U$ gives $T(Qf)\circ\beta_K=\beta_{K'}\circ Q\Gamma(u(U),f)$. These transformations descend to the homotopy category: additive functors send a homotopy $h$ to a homotopy, by applying the functor to $f-f'=dh+hd$. Apply clause (1) of the right-derived-plus-injective theorem to $v=\Gamma(u(U),-)$, $G=T$ and this $\beta$. It gives a unique natural transformation $\tau:S\to T$ satisfying $\tau_{QK}\circ\alpha^{u(U)}_K=\beta_K$ for every $K$. In particular its naturality holds for all derived morphisms, including those not represented by a complex map.

proof.text: Let $I,J,r$ be as stated. Naturality of the comparison unit on $\mathcal C$, applied to $r:LI\to J$, is $R\Gamma(U,Qr)\circ\alpha^U_{LI}=\alpha^U_J\circ Q\Gamma(U,r)$. The localization inverts the quasi-isomorphism $r$, and a functor preserves its inverse. Multiply this equality on the left by $R\Gamma(U,(Qr)^{-1})$ and on the right by $Q(e_I^{-1})$. Step 2 with $K=I$ is precisely the displayed replacement formula of the statement. Clause (2) of the right-derived theorem makes $\alpha^{u(U)}_I$ and $\alpha^U_J$ isomorphisms. This computes ordinary derived section pullback: apply the ordinary section map $e_I^{-1}$, apply the target replacement $r$ on sections, and identify the resolved target with $LI$ by $(Qr)^{-1}$. Only $Qr$ is inverted in this calculation.

proof.text:
Every $M$ has an isomorphism $\rho:QI\cong M$ with $I$ bounded below and injective by the injective-representative theorem, using enough injectives from step 1. Naturality gives explicitly
$$\tau_M=T(\rho)\circ\alpha^U_{LI}\circ Q(e_I^{-1})\circ(\alpha^{u(U)}_I)^{-1}\circ S(\rho^{-1}).$$
For every choice $I,\rho$, the right side equals the already constructed $\tau_M$; step 3 makes it independent of $J,r$ as well. For a coefficient morphism $a:M\to N$, naturality from step 2 is $T(a)\circ\tau_M=\tau_N\circ S(a)$, so the formula is compatible with arbitrary derived coefficient morphisms without choosing chain representatives for $a$.

Finally choose other right-derived pairs with units, writing $S',R\Gamma'(U,-)$ and $\tau'$. Clause (3) of the right-derived theorem gives unique unit-compatible natural isomorphisms $s:S\cong S'$ and $b:R\Gamma(U,-)\cong R\Gamma'(U,-)$; write $t=bL:T\cong T'$. For each $K$, unit compatibility gives
$$(t\circ\tau)_{QK}\circ\alpha^{u(U)}_K=t_{QK}\circ\alpha^U_{LK}\circ Q(e_K^{-1})=\alpha'^U_{LK}\circ Q(e_K^{-1})=(\tau'\circ s)_{QK}\circ\alpha^{u(U)}_K.$$
Clause (1), with target $T'$, implies $t\circ\tau=\tau'\circ s$. This proves invariance under precisely the uniquely isomorphic, unit-compatible choices specified in the statement.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q120-34d7be9a3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: No new nodes and the statement is unchanged. I read all five steps against the cited statements. Step 1: the site-sheaves node gives abelian with enough injectives; sites-and-cohomology (2) gives Γ additive; the continuous-cocontinuous topos adjunction gives g^{-1}=precomposition, so e is the additive identity on sections; geometric-inverse-image-exact, with the sites swapped, makes L exact, so termwise L preserves quasi-isomorphisms and bounded-below complexes. Step 2: clause (1) of lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective with v=Γ(u(U),−) and G=RΓ(U,−)∘L; β_K=α^U_{LK}Q(e_K^{-1}) is typed correctly and natural on K^+, so τ exists and is unique. Step 3: naturality of α^U at r, with Qr inverted by the localization, gives the replacement formula with the correct orientation. Clause (2) is applied only to α^{u(U)}_I and α^U_J; LI is never claimed injective and QΓ(U,r) is never inverted. Step 4: dplus-injective-representative (1) supplies (I,ρ), and the transport formula is correct. Step 5: clause (3) gives s and b, and uniqueness in (1) gives tτ=τ's. Source: Stacks sites-cohomology.tex l.9511 (0DD8), bounded-below injective route; the item is its canonical-map normalization, which the parent's step 4 uses exactly. Edge cases checked: u=id, r=id, zero complexes. No duplicate: the sibling lem-trf-site-injective-sections-model only gives the a/b isomorphisms. No cycle and no SGA. The declared tool use of the continuous-cocontinuous adjunction is accepted, since seven trace-formula nodes already use it and the unit has no equivalent node.
